paragraphs: R' Yannai, brother of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.
[Ketubot 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.21b.1) reads Rabbanai; [Ketubot 50b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.50b.5) reads Rabbi Benaah. Hyman identifies them all as the same person.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The equation of Yannai, Rabbanai and Benaah is Hyman’s own identification.

Sanhedrin 74b has Rav Yannai, brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. Berakhot 21b and Ketubot 21b read Rabbanai, without a separate title, while Ketubot 50b reads Rabbi Bannai, beside Hyman's Benaah. The abbreviated R' preserves the abbreviated ר׳ of Hyman's heading without choosing a full title over the witness's Rav. Hyman's equation of the names remains his identification.

Rabbanai transmits a ruling in Shmuel’s name at Ketubot 21b. Heilprin’s [Yannai notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2072&lang=en) cites the Sanhedrin form, while his [Rabbanai notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3217&lang=en) records the Berakhot and Ketubot forms. The texts share the brother’s name; the equation remains Hyman’s.
